Now, House Democrats are preparing to make Elon Musk a major target of congressional investigations if they regain control of the House in the midterms.

Also in previous years, Tesla stores, vehicles, and Superchargers were targeted by arson, vandalism, and gunfire. Political disagreements are never an excuse for violence. These are crimes, not legitimate forms of protest.

It's remarkable how much the relationship between Elon Musk and the Democratic Party has changed.

quote.name: Austin Justice
quote.text:
UPDATE: Alonzo Mabry is dead.

In March, the 62-year-old was using a computer at Austin's Central Library when the man next to him, Daniel Vasquez, stood up, hit him in the head, and stomped on his skull while he lay unconscious. Then Vasquez went back to his computer.

Mabry died in hospice and Vasquez was charged with murder last week.

Before the library, Vasquez had punched a CapMetro bus driver in the mouth. That was dismissed by prosecutors.

He also punched a mother in the face in front of her 11-year-old son, then punched the woman who tried to stop him. Those were also dismissed.

DA Jose Garza's office sent him to a six-month rehab program instead. He finished in June 2025 and every charge was wiped and he went back to the street.

posts.text:
Elon Musk says SpaceX is using its rocket-engine casting shop to make turbine blades and vanes, the parts that run 12 to 18 months behind the rest of the turbine, so it can bring power online 12 to 18 months faster than anyone else

“So we’re casting the blades and vanes for the turbines. So SpaceX already has a very advanced castings capability that was developed for rocket engines."

"So we have, I think, actually the most advanced casting capability on Earth, because the demands for castings for rocket engines exceed the demands for anything else you could possibly imagine."

"So, taking that incredible team that has, I think, objectively the most advanced casting technology in the world and saying, hey, can you guys also make some blades and vanes for terrestrial turbines is much easier than what they have done in the past."

"And when we talk to the turbine suppliers, they tell us that the blades and vanes are 12 to 18 months behind the rest of the turbine. Meaning they can deliver everything except the blades and vanes 12 to 18 months before they can deliver the blades and vanes."

"So casting is this really difficult bottleneck. And if anything, it seems to be getting worse."

"So that means that we can bring power online 12 to 18 months faster than anyone else."

"That’s the kind of advantage that’s difficult to replicate. Unless someone else is building an advanced casting shop, they will be unable to compete with SpaceX in this regard.”

quote.author: firesidealpha
quote.name: Fireside Alpha
quote.text:
Elon Musk reveals chip-fab "breakthroughs" he won’t discuss on the earnings call, says TeraFab’s first test chip is due around May or June next year with volume production around Q3'28, and credits ASML for “accelerating equipment deliveries”

“Well, I mean, we’re just figuring out chip fabrication. So, but I’ll tell you what our internal expectations are, which obviously I put, you know, big error bars in this because we don’t know if we will actually achieve this or not, but it’s what we’re aiming for internally: is to make our first sort of test chip functional in approximately May or June of next year."

"That’s just kind of a SRAM chip or something to basically test the line. That’s at the Research Fab in Austin."

"And we’re aiming to, our aspiration is to reach volume production around Q3 of ‘28 at TeraFab, at Gibbons Creek, the main TeraFab location. These were very aggressive dates, and we’re very appreciative of ASML and all of our other suppliers in accelerating equipment deliveries in order to achieve this outcome."

"Let’s just say that that outcome of achieving volume production is at least in the set of possible outcomes for Q3 or Q4 of ‘28. So these are obviously like insanely fast timeframes for chip production."

"We do have, I think, some significant potential breakthroughs in chip fabrication, but I don’t think I should discuss that on earnings call.”

"Let’s not give away the shop here. But I am optimistic that we will dramatically accelerate chip production and that TeraFab will ultimately do what the name suggests, which is to make a terawatt of superintelligence chips per year.”
